The P2P Bazaar

How most of the world actually buys crypto: directly from another human, with the coins locked in escrow until the money arrives. Modeled on real P2P marketplaces — offers, payment methods, escrow, trader chat, disputes — every trader here is a bot and every dollar is paper, so you can live the full lifecycle before ever risking a real one.

🔐 Escrow first. The seller's crypto locks in a simulated 2-of-3 multisig before any money moves. 🧾 Proof everything. Completed trades are sealed into your SHA-256 proof ledger like any other trade. ⚖️ Disputes exist. Try one on purpose — an arbitrator bot walks you through how it really works.

the lifecycle · escrow · safety

How a P2P trade actually works

No exchange sits in the middle — just two strangers, a smart-contract escrow, and a payment rail. Here's the exact path every trade in the bazaar walks, the same one billions of dollars move through on real P2P desks each month.

01🤝Match & lock

Taker hits an offer. The maker's crypto instantly locks into a 2-of-3 escrow — neither side can touch it, and the price is now fixed for the window.

→
02💸Pay off-chain

The buyer sends fiat by the agreed rail — bank transfer, UPI, Wise, cash — and marks it paid. The clock is the buyer's protection.

→
03✅Confirm & release

Seller sees the money land and releases escrow. Coins hit the buyer's wallet. If they ghost, the window expiring opens a dispute.

→
04⚖️Dispute if needed

An arbitrator reads the chat and payment proof, then awards escrow to the honest party. Reputation moves with the verdict.

Payment methods, decoded
Bank / SEPA / UPIlow risk

Traceable, reversible only by fraud claim. The everyday rail — slow to clear, hard to fake.

Wise · Revolut · N26medium

Fast and global, but accounts can freeze on flagged flows. Read the trader's terms.

PayPal · Zelle · Cash Appchargeback

Instant, but buyer-side reversible for months. Sellers price this in — or refuse it outright.

Gift cards · cash-in-personhigh risk

Irreversible and anonymous — the classic scam vectors. Deep escrow and reputation matter most here.

Stay-safe checklist
  • Never release before the money truly clears. "Sent" in an app is not "settled" in your bank. Pending ≠ paid.
  • Keep every message in the trade chat. Off-platform contact is the #1 scam tell — arbitrators only see what's on the record.
  • Match the name. The paying account should match the trader's verified identity. Third-party payments invite reversals.
  • Read reputation, not just the rate. A 99% trader at +0.5% beats a fresh account at spot. Completion rate is the real price.
  • Small first, then scale. A new counterparty earns trust one cleared trade at a time — exactly how the leaderboard is built.

In the real world P2P marketplaces list 300+ payment methods — from bank wires to M-Pesa to gift cards. The bazaar simulates the most common ones with realistic terms. Educational simulation only.

the monument

Satoshi Nakamoto

No photograph exists. No voice recording. No confirmed name. The only portrait that can honestly be made of Bitcoin's creator is this one — a figure assembled from decentralized nodes, the network that outlived its architect.

📜 Oct 31, 2008 — the whitepaper, nine pages ⛏ Jan 3, 2009 — the genesis block 👻 2011 — "moved on to other things"; silence since ₿ ~1,000,000 BTC mined early — never spent 🔍 identity: unknown — every candidate has denied it

Every dot is a node; every line, a connection. Rotate him and he dissolves into pure network — which is, perhaps, the point.
